label: late original steps / delimiter (t>=7) in long sequences, gated by first token p/o/r/m/a/i or input e/y/v/n
explanation: Fires only at steps t=5..9, on the last original tokens and the <DEL> step, and never in the copy phase or at t<=4. It is effectively limited to long sequences (L=8-9 hold 96% of the mass). The rate climbs toward the end of the input: 23% at orig_idx 8, 5% at <DEL>. The position window alone has 92% recall but only 12% precision. Within the window, firing depends on content: it is much more likely when the first original token is p, o, r, m, a or i (lift 2-4.6x, ranked roughly in that order) and when the current input is e, y, v or n. The largest activations (0.9-1.0 of max) fall on an e/y/n input at the last original position, with the following <DEL> at about 0.7. Repeated inputs (in_first=0) rarely fire it. The content gating looks like a distributed code, not a clean rule, so precision stays around 0.35.
